title: Patient Payment Plans Servicing Limits: Modifications, Due-Day Changes and Term Extension
content:
The servicing limits of each Patient Payment Plans tier cap how often a plan may be modified, how often its due day may change, and whether and how far its term may be lengthened.

| Tier | Maximum modifications over the plan's life | Maximum due-day changes over the plan's life | Term may be lengthened on request | Maximum total months the term may be lengthened |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Month Interest-Free Plan | 3 | 1 | No | 0 |
| 6-Month Interest-Free Plan | 3 | 1 | No | 0 |
| 12-Month Interest-Free Plan | 4 | 2 | Yes | 6 |
| 18-Month Extended Plan | 4 | 2 | Yes | 6 |
| 24-Month Extended Plan | 4 | 2 | No | 0 |
| Financial Hardship Plan | 6 | 2 | Yes | 12 |

Scope of the columns:

- A *modification* is any change of installment, due day, method, term or pause.
- The term-extension maximum is a total over the plan's life, in months.

Observations drawn from the table:

- Term extension is available on the 12-Month Interest-Free Plan and the 18-Month Extended Plan up to 6 months in total, and on the Financial Hardship Plan up to 12 months in total; the 3-Month and 6-Month Interest-Free Plans and the 24-Month Extended Plan show No and 0.
- The two shortest tiers allow 1 due-day change; every other tier allows 2.
